title: Do You Secretly Feel Like a Fraud at Church?
subtitle: Everyone around you seems so sure, so spiritual. And there you are, wondering if you're faking it. You're not alone.

questions.text: When you're sitting in church, the quiet thought underneath is often...

options.text: I believe this, so why do I still feel like a fake?
I know exactly how to look the part by now.
I'm not sure I even believe what they're all singing.
I'm so tired from serving I can barely focus.

questions.text: When people see you as a 'strong Christian,' you feel...

options.text: Like a fraud who's got everyone fooled.
Comfortable. The role fits, even if it's a performance.
Awkward, because privately I'm full of questions.
Trapped, because now I can't admit I'm running empty.

questions.text: Where does the 'fraud' feeling really come from for you?

options.text: My insides don't match the faith I actually have.
I've gotten good at playing a part I don't always feel.
I have doubts I'd never say out loud here.
I keep serving on fumes and smiling through it.

questions.text: If you said the most honest thing in your small group, it'd be...

options.text: "I love God but I always feel like I'm not enough here."
"Half of what I say in here is the right answer, not my real one."
"I'm honestly not sure I believe some of this anymore."
"I'm exhausted and I don't know how to stop."

questions.text: How do you compare yourself to others at church?

options.text: Everyone seems more genuine and 'real' than me.
I'm great at matching whatever spiritual vibe is expected.
They seem so certain, and I'm full of question marks.
They look rested. I look fine but I'm wrecked.

questions.text: What do you do with the parts of you that don't fit the image?

options.text: Hide them and hope nobody looks too closely.
Tuck them behind the role I play so well.
Sit on my doubts silently and nod along.
Push through and tell myself rest is for later.
That if they really knew me, they'd see I don't measure up.
That if I drop the act, I won't know who I really am.
That my doubts make me unwelcome here.
That if I stop serving, I'll have no value here.

questions.text: When you do something genuinely good for God, how does it feel?

options.text: Like an impostor who somehow pulled it off again.
Like another good performance landed well.
Hollow, because I'm not even sure I believe.
Honestly meaningful, even if I'm hard on myself.

questions.text: Deep down, what do you most need to hear?

options.text: You're not a fraud. I see the real faith in you.
You can stop performing. I love the unscripted you.
Your honest questions don't scare Me. Bring them.
You're harder on yourself than I am. Come and rest.

the-impostor.name: The Impostor
the-impostor.description: You genuinely believe, and yet you walk around church feeling like a fake who's about to be found out. Here's the thing: that gap between your insides and the image isn't proof you're a fraud. It's proof you're human, and probably more honest than the people who seem so sure. God isn't grading the performance. He sees real faith in you, the kind that keeps showing up even while it doubts itself. You belong here more than you think.

scripture.text: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.

the-performer.name: The Performer
the-performer.description: You've gotten really good at playing the part: the right words, the right face, the expected spiritual answer. It works, but it's lonely, because nobody is actually meeting you. God isn't asking for the polished version. He already knows the unscripted you, the doubts and the off days, and He wants that person, not the role. You can lay the act down. The relationship you're hungry for starts the moment you stop performing for it.

scripture.text: Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.

the-quiet-doubter.name: The Quiet Doubter
the-quiet-doubter.description: You carry questions you'd never dare raise out loud, so you nod along and feel like a fraud for it. But doubt isn't the opposite of faith. It's often a sign that your faith is alive enough to wrestle. The disciples doubted right in front of Jesus, and He didn't throw them out. He met them in it. Your questions don't disqualify you. Bring them honestly to God. He'd rather have your real doubts than your fake certainty.

scripture.text: And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted.

the-burned-out-server.name: The Burned-Out Server
the-burned-out-server.description: You feel like a fraud because you're smiling and serving on an empty tank, and you can't admit how depleted you really are. But your value at church was never your output. You're not a fraud for being tired. You're a person who's been giving more than you've received. God isn't standing over you asking for more. He's inviting you to come sit down and be filled. It's okay to stop, rest, and let yourself be cared for too.

scripture.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

the-real-deal.name: The Real Deal
the-real-deal.description: Plot twist: you're not actually a fraud at all. You're just far harder on yourself than God is. The fact that you worry about being fake is itself a sign of a sincere heart, because phonies rarely lose sleep over authenticity. Your faith is real, even on the days it feels small. Try seeing yourself the way God sees you, with grace instead of suspicion. You're not faking it. You're the genuine article, flaws and all, and He's pleased with you.

scripture.text: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.
